label: Level 1 · Meeting people — a hotel check-in
lines: Level one. You will hear a conversation at a hotel. Listen and complete the form.
Good afternoon, and welcome to the Riverside Hotel. How can I help you?
Hello. I've got a booking for tonight. My surname is Thompson.
Lovely. Could you spell your surname for me, please?
T. H. O. M. P. S. O. N.
Thank you. And what's your first name?
People often write my first name wrong, so I'll spell it for you.
S. T. E. V. E. N.
Perfect, thank you. Your room is number two one four. It's on the second floor.
Room two one four. That's great, thank you.
Can I have a phone number, please?
Of course. It's oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, one two three.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, one two three?
Thank you. And where are you from?
I'm from Brighton, on the south coast. I'm here for work this week.
How nice. And you're staying with us for three nights, is that right?
Yes, that's right, three nights. What time is breakfast in the morning?
Breakfast starts at seven thirty, in the restaurant on the ground floor.
Lovely. And where can I leave my car?
Our car park is behind the hotel, on Kingsley Street.
Sorry, could you spell the name of the street for me?
K. I. N. G. S. L. E. Y.
Thanks. Is there a shop near here? I need a few things.
Yes, there's a big supermarket opposite the hotel. It's open until ten in the evening.
That's very useful. And what time is check-out on my last day?
Check-out is at eleven o'clock in the morning. Here's your key, and enjoy your stay!
Thank you very much. You've been very kind.

label: Level 2 · Family & friends — joining a sports club
lines: Level two. You will hear a conversation at a sports club. Listen and complete the form.
Good morning, Greenfield Sports Club. How can I help you?
Hello. I'd like to join the club with my son, please. He's very keen on sport.
Wonderful. I'll fill in the form for you. What's your surname, please?
My surname is Hughes. I'll spell it for you.
H. U. G. H. E. S.
Thank you. And what's your first name?
Lovely. And what's your son's name?
His name is Callum. People often spell it wrong, so here it is.
C. A. double L. U. M.
Thanks. And how old is Callum?
He's nine years old, and he's got lots of energy!
I'm sure he has! Which sport would he like to do?
He wants to learn swimming. His best friend goes to your swimming club too.
Great. Our swimming lessons for children are on Saturday mornings.
Saturday is perfect for us. We're free at the weekend.
Good. Now, can I have your address, please?
Yes, we live at eighteen Hampton Road.
Could you spell the name of the road for me?
H. A. M. P. T. O. N.
Thank you. And what's the best phone number for you?
It's oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, four five two.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, four five two?
Perfect. For you and Callum together, it's thirty pounds a month.
That sounds fine. Do we need anything for the first lesson?
Yes, please bring a photo of Callum for his membership card.
No problem. Thank you very much for your help.

label: Level 3 · My home — renting a room
lines: Level three. You will hear a phone call about a room to rent. Listen and complete the notes.
Hello. I'm calling about the room in your advert. Is it still free?
Yes, it is. I'm the owner of the house. My name is Mrs Fletcher.
Sorry, could you spell your name for me, please?
F. L. E. T. C. H. E. R.
Thank you. And where is the house?
It's at twenty-seven Ashford Street, near the town centre.
Could you spell the name of the street, please?
A. S. H. F. O. R. D.
Thanks. And where's the room in the house?
It's on the top floor. It's quiet, and it has a lovely view of the garden.
That sounds nice. Is there any furniture in the room?
Yes, there's a bed, a desk and a big wardrobe for your clothes.
Great. How much is the rent?
The rent is four hundred and fifty pounds a month. That includes the bills.
That's fine for me. Do I share the bathroom?
Yes, you share it with two other people. They're both students, and they're very tidy.
And what's near the house? I like going running.
There's a big park at the end of the street. It's perfect for running.
Can I come and see the room this week?
Yes, of course. Come on Thursday evening, after six o'clock.
Thursday is good for me. What's your phone number, in case I'm late?
My mobile number is oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, seven one eight.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, seven one eight?
Thank you very much, Mrs Fletcher. See you on Thursday.

label: Level 4 · My day — a doctor's appointment
lines: Level four. You will hear a phone call to a doctor's surgery. Listen and complete the notes.
Good morning, Oakfield Surgery. How can I help you?
Hello. I'd like to make an appointment with a doctor, please.
Of course. Can I have your surname, please?
Yes, it's Lawson. I'll spell it for you.
L. A. W. S. O. N.
Thank you, Mrs Lawson. Which doctor do you usually see?
Doctor Carter. Let me just check the spelling on my computer.
C. A. R. T. E. R.
Yes, that's right. She's very good.
I've had a bad headache every afternoon this week. I think I'm working too hard.
I'm sorry to hear that. Doctor Carter is free on Monday at three thirty.
Monday is difficult for me. I work in an office until four o'clock, and on Mondays we always have a long meeting.
No problem. What about Wednesday? She is free at four fifteen.
Wednesday at four fifteen is perfect. I finish work at four, and the surgery is only five minutes from my office.
Great. Her room is on the first floor. It's room twelve.
Room twelve, on the first floor. Do I need to bring anything?
Yes, please bring any medicine you take at the moment.
I'll bring it with me, then.
And please arrive ten minutes early, because there's a short form to fill in.
That's fine. Can I have the surgery's phone number, in case I'm late?
Yes, it's oh one six three two, nine six oh, four seven one.
Oh one six three two, nine six oh, four seven one?
Thank you. And where can I park? I'll come by car.
Our car park is very small, so it's better to park next to the library. It's just across the road.
Thank you very much for your help. See you on Wednesday.

label: Level 5 · Food & cafés — ordering for a party
lines: Level five. You will hear a phone call to a café. Listen and complete the order form.
Hello, Sunflower Café. Jessica speaking. How can I help you?
Hi. I'd like to order some food for my daughter's birthday party, please.
How lovely! Can I take your surname first?
Yes, it's Barton. I'll spell it for you.
B. A. R. T. O. N.
Thank you, Mr Barton. When is the party?
It's on Sunday afternoon, here at the café.
Good, Sunday is a quiet day for us. How many children are coming?
About twenty children, and a few parents too.
We've got a lovely garden room at the back. It's big and sunny.
Perfect. What food do you have for children?
Most children love our cheese and tomato pizzas.
Pizzas sound great. How much are they?
They're eight pounds each, and one pizza is enough for three children.
That's good. But one boy can't eat cheese. Have you got anything else?
Yes, we can make some chicken sandwiches for him.
Lovely. And can you make a birthday cake?
Of course. Our chocolate cake is very popular. What name would you like on it?
Please write Rosie. That's my daughter's name.
That's a beautiful name. So the total is one hundred and twenty pounds.
That's fine. Can I pay on the day?
Yes, you can. Can I have a phone number, please?
Sure. It's oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, three six five.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, three six five?
Thank you, Mr Barton. We will see you and Rosie on Sunday!

label: Level 6 · Shopping — a lost bag at a shop
lines: Level six. You will hear a woman phoning a department store about a lost bag. Listen and complete the form.
Good morning, Westgate Department Store. Customer service. How can I help you?
Hello. I think I left my bag in your shop. Has anyone found it?
I can check for you. What's your surname, please?
It's Palmer. I'll spell it for you.
P. A. L. M. E. R.
Thank you, Mrs Palmer. When were you in the shop?
I was here on Saturday morning, with my sister.
And where do you think you left the bag?
In the shoe department. I tried on some boots, and I put my bag on the floor.
I see. What does the bag look like?
It's a small leather bag. It's dark green, with a long strap.
There's a red purse inside it.
Is there any money in the purse?
Is there anything else in the bag?
Yes, there's a pair of sunglasses in a black case.
Good news, Mrs Palmer. I think we've got your bag here! Can I have your address, please?
Of course. I live at forty-two Ashby Road. I'll spell Ashby for you.
Thank you. And what's your phone number?
It's oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, eight four six.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, eight four six?
Can I come and get my bag today?
Yes, of course. You can collect it from the information desk on the ground floor.
Please bring something with your name on it, like your driving licence.
Thank you so much! I'll come this afternoon.

label: Level 7 · My town — at the tourist office
lines: Level seven. You will hear a man at a tourist office. He is asking about places in the town. Listen and complete the notes.
Good morning, and welcome to the tourist office. How can I help you?
Hello. I'm here on holiday, and I'd like to see the town. Can you help me?
Of course. Can I have your name, please? Then I can book a town walk for you.
Yes, it's Barton. I'll spell it for you.
B. A. R. T. O. N.
Thank you, Mr Barton. How long are you staying in town?
I'm here until Sunday. I go home on Sunday evening.
Lovely. What would you like to see first?
I'd like to visit the museum. Where is it?
The town museum is on Morley Street, next to the library. I'll spell Morley for you.
M. O. R. L. E. Y.
Thank you. And what time does it open?
It opens at nine thirty every morning.
Is the museum open every day?
No, it isn't. It's closed on Mondays.
OK. And how much is a ticket?
A ticket for an adult is six pounds.
Great. Is there a good place for lunch near the museum?
Yes, try the Old Mill café. It's by the river, and the soup is lovely.
Thank you. What about the castle? When does it close?
The castle closes at five o'clock, so go in the morning or early afternoon.
There's also a free town walk on Saturday morning. Would you like to come?
Yes, please! Where does it start?
It starts in the market square, at ten o'clock.
And can I phone you if I have a question?
Of course. Our phone number is oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, five nine three.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, five nine three?
Thank you very much for your help. Goodbye!
Goodbye, Mr Barton, and enjoy your stay!

label: Level 8 · Free time — signing up for a course
lines: Level eight. You will hear a woman at a community centre. She wants to sign up for a course. Listen and complete the form.
Good evening, and welcome to Hillside Community Centre. How can I help you?
Hello. I'd like to sign up for a course, please. I want to do something new in my free time.
Great. Which course are you interested in?
I want to do the photography course. I saw it on your website.
Photography for Beginners. That's a very popular course. Can I have your surname, please?
Yes, it's Dalton. I'll spell it for you.
D. A. L. T. O. N.
Thank you, Ms Dalton. And what's your address?
I live at number twelve, Penford Road. I'll spell Penford for you.
P. E. N. F. O. R. D.
Thank you. There are two groups for this course. One meets on Tuesday afternoon, and the other meets on Thursday evening. Which day is better for you?
I work in the afternoons, so Thursday is better for me.
No problem. The Thursday class starts at seven thirty in the evening.
And how long is the course?
It's eight weeks long, and each class is two hours.
Great. How much does it cost?
It's forty-five pounds for the whole course.
Do I need to bring a camera?
No, you don't. You can take photos with your phone. But please bring a notebook to write in.
OK. And where are the classes?
They're on the second floor, in the big room at the end.
And can I phone you if I can't come one week?
Of course. Our phone number is oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, two six four.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, two six four?
Thank you very much. See you on Thursday!
See you on Thursday, Ms Dalton. Enjoy the course!

label: Step 1 · Hello! — a new student at an English club
lines: Step one. You will hear a teacher and a new student at an English club. Listen and write the answers.
Hello, and welcome to the English club! I'm your teacher. My name is Kate.
Hello, Kate. Nice to meet you. How do you spell your name, please?
Thank you. And what's your name?
My name is Sam. I'll spell it for you.
Thank you, Sam. How old are you?
And where are you from, Sam?
I'm from London. I live here with my family.
Have you got a brother or a sister?
Yes, I've got a brother. His name is Tom.
Our classroom is room nine. It's next to the library.
There are fourteen students in our class.
Fourteen students? That's a nice class.
Our lesson starts at four o'clock.
Now, please open your book at page five.
Page five? OK, I've got it.

label: Step 2 · Numbers 1–20 — a new student at a school office
lines: Step two. You will hear a new student at a school office. Listen and write the answers.
Hello. Are you a new student?
Yes, I am. My name is Ben Hart.
Can you spell your first name, please?
Thank you. And can you spell your surname?
Thank you, Ben. How old are you?
It's oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, five one seven.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, five one seven?
This is your locker. It's number eleven.
Do you come to school by bus?
Yes, I do. I come on bus number twenty.
There are nineteen students in your class.
Nineteen students? That's a big class.
You have six lessons every day.
Your English teacher is in room fourteen.
Room fourteen. Thank you very much.
You're welcome, Ben. Have a good day.

label: Step 3 · My family — a family photo
lines: Step three. You will hear a girl talking about a family photo. Listen and write the answers.
Is this a photo of your family?
Yes, it is. This is my brother. His name is Jack.
Ten years old? He's very tall.
And who is this little girl?
This is my sister. Her name is Mia. I'll spell it for you.
Six years old? She's very sweet.
This is my mum. Her name is Rose.
Yes, it is. My dad's name is Mark.
Who is the old woman with the cats?
That's my grandma. Her name is Ruby. I'll spell it for you.
Grandma has got two cats. She loves them.
Yes, it is. His name is Max.
Three years old? He's very young.
Yes, and he's very funny. We all love him.

label: Step 4 · Colours & things — a lost school bag
lines: Step four. You will hear a boy at a school office. He can't find his bag. Listen and write the answers.
Yes, please. I can't find my school bag.
My first name is Luke. I'll spell it for you.
Thank you, Luke. What colour is your bag?
It's blue. It's a big blue bag.
And there's a yellow star on it.
There are three books in it. They're my English books.
There's a green pencil case too.
Yes, and there are four pens in it.
There's an apple, and there's a black hat.
An apple and a black hat?
Look, I've got a blue bag here. A teacher found it in room sixteen.
Room sixteen? That's my classroom. Yes, that's my bag!

label: Step 5 · Numbers 20–100 — phoning a sports shop
lines: Step five. You will hear a woman phoning a sports shop. Listen and write the answers.
Hello, City Sports. How can I help you?
Hello. How much is a football, please?
And how much is a sports bag?
A sports bag is forty pounds.
I need some trainers for my son. How much are they?
We've got football T-shirts too. They're twenty-two pounds.
And how much is a tennis racket?
This tennis racket is a hundred pounds.
A hundred pounds? Oh no, that's too much.
OK. I'd like the trainers, please. Can you keep them for me?
Yes, of course. What's your name, please?
My first name is Anna. I'll spell it for you.
It's oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, two eight one.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, two eight one?
And what's the shop's phone number, please?
Yes. It's oh one six three two, nine six oh, five three nine.
Oh one six three two, nine six oh, five three nine?
Yes, that's right. See you soon!

label: Step 6 · Days & times — a sports centre
lines: Step six. You will hear a girl at a sports centre. She asks about classes. Listen and write the answers.
Yes, please. I want to join a class after school.
My first name is Lucy. I'll spell it for you.
Thank you, Lucy. There's swimming on Monday.
On Monday? Great. I love swimming.
Is there a dance class too?
Yes. Dance is on Wednesday, at six o'clock.
And when is the tennis class?
Tennis is on Saturday morning, at ten o'clock.
Is the sports centre open on Sunday?
No, sorry. We're closed on Sunday.
What time do you open in the morning?
You're welcome. See you on Monday, Lucy!

label: Step 7 · Food — ordering food at a café
lines: Step seven. You will hear a woman ordering food at a café. Listen and write the answers.
Hello. My son likes pizza. How much is a small pizza?
A small pizza is six pounds.
Six pounds? OK, one small pizza, please.
My daughter likes fish. Have you got fish and chips?
Yes, we have. Fish and chips is eight pounds.
I'd like a chicken salad, please.
A chicken salad is five pounds.
Yes. Two orange juices and a cup of tea, please.
Two orange juices and a tea. OK.
Thank you. Can I have your name for the order?
Yes. My first name is Jane. I'll spell it for you.
Thank you, Jane. Your food is ready in ten minutes.

label: Step 8 · Animals & pets — a girl at the vet's
lines: Step eight. You will hear a girl at the vet's. She talks about her pets. Listen and write the answers.
Hello. I've got a new dog. Can the vet see him today?
Yes, of course. What's your dog's name?
His name is Rex. I'll spell it for you.
Have you got any other pets?
Yes, I've got a cat. Her name is Luna. I'll spell it for you.
She's nine. She's an old cat.
She's black, and she has got green eyes.
A black cat with green eyes. Beautiful!
Three fish! You've got a lot of pets.
The vet can see Rex at four o'clock today.
Four o'clock. Thank you very much!

label: Step 9 · My room — a room at a summer school
lines: Step nine. You will hear a girl at a summer school. A man shows her the room. Listen and write the answers.
Hello. Welcome to our summer school. What's your name?
Hi. My first name is Beth. I'll spell it for you.
Thank you, Beth. You're in room twelve.
There's another girl in your room. Her name is Tess.
Here's the room. Your bed is next to the window.
There's a desk too, and the lamp is on the desk.
Where can I put my clothes?
In the cupboard. It's behind the door.
Is there a mirror in the room?
Yes, there's a mirror on the wall.
They're under your bed, in a blue box.
Under the bed, in a blue box. Thanks.
Dinner is at six o'clock, in the big room downstairs.
Six o'clock. Thank you very much!

label: Step 10 · My friend — a new friend
lines: Step ten. You will hear a boy and his mum. They talk about his new friend. Listen and write the answers.
Dan, I want to write a party card for your new friend. What's his name?
His first name is Nick. I'll spell it for you.
He likes football. He plays every Saturday.
He's got a little sister. She's seven years old.
And what food does he like?
He loves pasta, but he doesn't like cheese.
Have you got his phone number?
Yes. It's oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, six three nine.
Oh seven seven double oh, nine double oh, six three nine?
Good. I'll call his mum about your party on Friday.
